chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: mean across regions weighted by ASAP's own cropland area, km2_crop
aggregate.caveat: weighted by cropland area, so Villa Clara carries 10% of this figure and the smallest regions barely move it. The national number is mostly its largest crop region by construction.

severity.statement: The 4th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 18 of the 165 published countries, about one in nine, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.193, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for

rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: mean across regions weighted by ASAP's own cropland area, km2_crop
aggregate.caveat: weighted by cropland area, so Central carries 65% of this figure and the smallest regions barely move it. The national number is mostly its largest crop region by construction.

severity.statement: The 26th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 18 of the 165 published countries, about one in nine, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.206, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 5th steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 5th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: mean across regions weighted by ASAP's own cropland area, km2_crop
aggregate.caveat: weighted by cropland area, so Aran carries 41% of this figure and the smallest regions barely move it. The national number is mostly its largest crop region by construction.

severity.statement: The 24th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 18 of the 165 published countries, about one in nine, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.22, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 21st of 26 by fall steepness, from the 1st highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 21st of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: mean across regions weighted by ASAP's own cropland area, km2_crop
aggregate.caveat: this country figure IS Bhutan, which is the country's only crop region. There is no weighting choice to make.

severity.statement: The 22nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 18 of the 165 published countries, about one in nine, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.142, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.statement: The 2nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 26th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: mean across regions weighted by ASAP's own cropland area, km2_crop
aggregate.caveat: weighted by cropland area, so Masvingo carries 17% of this figure and the smallest regions barely move it. The national number is mostly its largest crop region by construction.

severity.statement: The joint 23rd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2021
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 18 of the 165 published countries, about one in nine, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.191, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26, but from the 1st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
